statements.markdown:
We first fix $0<T<1$, then a mesh $N\ge1$,
$\Delta=T/N$, $t_j=j\Delta$.
On independent standard normals $Z_1,\ldots,Z_{N+1}$, set
$$
Y_0=0,\quad Y_j=Y_{j-1}+\sqrt\Delta Z_j+
 \Delta\gamma(t_{j-1})u(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1}),
$$
$$
c_j=(\mathbb E a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})^2)^{-1/2},\qquad
g_j=c_ja(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})Z_j.
$$
For sufficiently large $N$, all $c_j$, $1\le j\le N$, are finite
and positive. Couple the increments to Brownian motion. On the fixed
strip, the gradient and curvature are bounded and Lipschitz. Monotonicity
gives, for the left-grid projection $\pi_N$,
$$
\int_0^T|\gamma(s)-\gamma(\pi_N(s))|\,ds
 \le\Delta(\gamma(T)-\gamma(0)).
$$
Drift error estimates and discrete Gronwall yield
$\mathbb E\max_{j\le N}|Y_j-X_{t_j}|^2\to0$, hence
$\max_j|c_j-1|\to0$. The $g_j$ are orthonormal in $L^2$:
they have unit variance and conditional mean zero given their past.
Their predictable multipliers may depend on earlier coordinates, so
orthonormality does not assert independence.
statements.section: 7. A finite Gaussian spin and its adjacent correlations

statements.markdown:
**The finite Gaussian input.** Fix the minimiser and its diffusion,
a cutoff $0<T<1$, and a mesh $t_j=j\Delta$, $\Delta=T/N$.
The mesh count $N$ is distinct from the number of spins $n$.
From independent standard normals $Z_1,\ldots,Z_{N+1}$, form
$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_0&=0,\\
Y_j&=Y_{j-1}+\sqrt\Delta Z_j+
       \Delta\gamma(t_{j-1})u(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1}),\\
h_j&=\frac{a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})}
 {\sqrt{\mathbb E a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})^2}},\qquad g_j=h_jZ_j
 \quad(1\leq j\leq N).
\end{aligned}
$$
[OpenAI (2026a), Proposition 7.2][FS] proves that the denominators
are positive for all sufficiently large $N$. Since $h_j$ depends
only on $Z_1,\ldots,Z_{j-1}$, the $g_j$ are centred and
orthonormal in $L^2$. They need not be independent Gaussians.
statements.section: 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit
